skill.name: agent-desktop
skill.description: Operate desktop applications on macOS, Windows, and Linux through native accessibility trees using the agent-desktop CLI. Inspect controls, fill forms, navigate menus, manage windows, and verify results.
skill.summary: Automate desktop applications through accessibility trees, scoped actions, and explicit verification.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: All 67 static findings are benign documentation matches, including Markdown backticks, keystroke delivery, local session storage, and loopback CDP endpoints. One semantic finding concerns pointer dispatch after inconclusive hit tests, which can misdirect input despite visibility checks. No evidence found of credential theft, covert keylogging, external exfiltration, or audit-directed prompt injection in the five reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Pointer delivery proceeds when the receives_events hit test is inconclusive.
remediation.suggestion: Reject unknown hit-test results before pointer dispatch, or require explicit user confirmation after presenting the target and uncertainty.

semantic_findings.title: Pointer Delivery Proceeds After Inconclusive Hit Tests
semantic_findings.description: The documentation states that receives_events fails open when a hit test is inconclusive. Pointer input can reach an obscuring control or window, causing unintended actions or disclosure of typed data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reference explicitly states that unknown hit-test results still dispatch input. The implementation was not supplied, so this finding concerns documented behavior.

content.user_title: Automate Desktop Apps With Accessibility Controls
content.value_statement: Desktop workflows often require repeated navigation, data entry, and checks across application windows. This skill guides agents through scoped accessibility actions and verification using agent-desktop.
actual_capabilities: Inspect accessibility trees, find controls by role or name, and read live element properties.
Click controls, enter text, select options, and set checkbox states with action-result verification.
Navigate native menus, dialogs, and overlays using snapshot-qualified element references.
Launch and close apps, manage windows, and wait for text, element, or lifecycle changes.
Capture screenshots, manage clipboard representations, and inspect supported notification surfaces.
Organize runs into sessions, inspect traces, and hand off Chromium web contents to an optional CDP client.
limitations: Requires the agent-desktop binary, an active desktop session, and the permissions required by each operating system.
Accessibility coverage and headless action support vary by app and platform; physical input requires explicit user permission.
A delivered action does not always prove application acceptance; batches are not transactions and uncertain actions need independent verification.
Clipboard data, notification bodies, and optional screenshot artifacts can contain sensitive information; loopback CDP allows same-user local control.

use_cases.title: Complete Repeated Desktop Forms
use_cases.description: Enter approved data into application fields, select options, and verify the completed form before submission.

use_cases.title: Check Desktop UI Workflows
use_cases.description: Inspect controls, exercise menus and dialogs, and distinguish verified changes from uncertain input delivery.

use_cases.title: Review Application Notifications
use_cases.description: List notifications from a selected app and act on specific entries only after checking their current fingerprints.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect an Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Check agent-desktop status and permissions, then inspect [app]. List its visible controls without changing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Form Without Submitting
prompt_templates.prompt: In [app], fill [fields] with [approved values]. Use current references and verify each field. Stop before submitting or enabling physical input.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: scoped data entry with verification.

prompt_templates.title: Navigate a Save Dialog
prompt_templates.prompt: In [app], save the current document to [approved destination]. Inspect each menu or dialog surface. Ask before overwriting files or using physical input.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: native menus and dialog handling.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Scoped Multi-Step Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Run [approved workflow] in [app] within a dedicated session. Use event waits and stop batches on errors. Verify uncertain deliveries before any repeat. Keep screenshot tracing off.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: session isolation, synchronization, and retry control.

output_examples.input: Inspect the active Notes window without changing it.
output_examples.output: Example report: The selected Notes window exposes a sidebar, a note list, and an editor. No controls were activated.

output_examples.input: Fill the contact form with approved details and stop before submission.
output: Example report: Name and email fields match the approved values.
The selected option was checked after entry.
The form remains open and was not submitted.

output_examples.input: A Save shortcut was delivered, but its wait timed out. Check before retrying.
output_examples.output: Example report: The save dialog is already open. The shortcut was not repeated. Confirmation is pending in the dialog.

best_practices: Check status and permissions, then scope reads and actions to the intended app, window, or overlay.
Use fresh qualified references, event waits, and independent state checks before repeating an uncertain action.
Require explicit permission for physical input and minimize sensitive artifacts, clipboard reads, and CDP exposure.
anti_patterns: Retrying a click, submission, or toggle merely because a wait timed out.
Switching to physical input after a headless refusal without explicit user permission.
Sharing unredacted screenshots, notifications, or clipboard contents, or running parallel writers against one editor.

faq.question: Which operating systems are supported?
faq.answer: The guide covers macOS, Windows, and Linux. Available surfaces, permissions, and action mechanisms vary by platform.

faq.question: Does this skill install the desktop tool?
faq.answer: No. It requires an available agent-desktop binary. Check status and load the platform reference before starting.

faq.question: Can it work without taking keyboard or mouse focus?
faq.answer: Supported semantic actions are headless by default. Physical gestures require headed mode and explicit user permission; some actions vary by operating system.

faq.question: Does success mean the application saved my changes?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Field verification proves the observed field value, not document acceptance. Check the application's resulting state independently.

faq.question: Are captured records always redacted?
faq.answer: No. Trace lines redact sensitive fields, but optional screenshot artifacts are unredacted. Notification output is verbatim, and clipboard reads may expose private data.

faq.question: Is a browser automation client required?
faq.answer: No. Accessibility is the default path. An optional CDP client can control freshly launched Chromium apps; close the debug-enabled app afterward.
